docs.title: json-config-qt
docs.text:
A Qt (PySide6) editor for the layers of a json-config LayeredConfig. It shows each layer's JSON as a tree with typed values, edits it with undo and redo, and writes the layer's file back.

from json_config_qt.editor_dialog import ConfigEditorDialog

dialog = ConfigEditorDialog.show_for(config, parent=main_window)
dialog.saved.connect(on_layer_saved)    # config.values is already refreshed
  • A dialog for a host application to open, or a widget to embed in its own UI.
  • A tree with an editor per type: spin boxes, check boxes, a color picker, text.
  • One undo history per layer, kept while you switch between layers.
  • Binary blobs (base64 strings) are hidden but always saved back untouched.
  • A standalone launcher to edit any set of JSON files.

def __init__(self, config: LayeredConfig, parent: QtCore.QObject | None = None):
    """Initialize the document.

    Args:
        config (LayeredConfig): The config whose layers are edited.
        parent (QtCore.QObject | None, optional): Parent object.
    """
    super().__init__(parent)
    self.config = config
    self.undo_group = QtGui.QUndoGroup(self)
    self._models: dict[str, JsonTreeModel] = {}
    self._current: str | None = None
    if config.layers:
        self.set_layer(config.layers[0])

def model_for(self, name: str) -> JsonTreeModel:
    """Return the tree model of a layer, creating it on first access.

    Args:
        name (str): The layer name.

    Returns:
        JsonTreeModel: The layer's model, holding its own undo stack.
    """
    if name not in self._models:
        stack = QtGui.QUndoStack(self)
        model = JsonTreeModel(stack, self)
        model.load(self.layer(name).get_data())
        stack.cleanChanged.connect(self.dirtyChanged)
        self.undo_group.addStack(stack)
        self._models[name] = model
    return self._models[name]

def new_layer(
    self,
    name: str,
    depends_on: str | None = None,
    file_path: pathlib.Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Register a new, empty layer and make it current.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a layer called *name* already exists or *depends_on* is
            not a registered layer.
    """
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("Layer name must not be empty.")
    if depends_on is not None and depends_on not in self.layers:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown layer '{depends_on}'")
    self.config.layer_manager.register(
        ConfigLayer(
            name=name,
            depends_on=[depends_on] if depends_on else [],
            file_path=pathlib.Path(file_path) if file_path else None,
        )
    )
    self.layersChanged.emit()
    self.set_layer(name)

def save_layer(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Write one layer to its file and refresh the config's resolved values.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: if the layer has no file path.
    """
    layer = self.layer(name)
    if layer.file_path is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Layer '{name}' has no file path.")
    model = self.model_for(name)
    layer.replace_data(model.to_python())
    self.config.layer_manager.save(name)
    model.undo_stack.setClean()
    self.config.resolve()
    self.saved.emit(name)

def set_layer(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Make *name* the current layer.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *name* is not a registered layer.
    """
    if name not in self.layers:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown layer '{name}'")
    if name == self._current:
        return
    self._current = name
    self.undo_group.setActiveStack(self.model_for(name).undo_stack)
    self.currentLayerChanged.emit(name)

@classmethod
def show_for(
    cls, config: LayeredConfig, parent: QtWidgets.QWidget | None = None
) -> ConfigEditorDialog:
    """Show the editor for *config*, reusing the open one if there is one.

    Args:
        config (LayeredConfig): The config whose layers are edited.
        parent (QtWidgets.QWidget | None, optional): Parent widget for a new dialog.

    Returns:
        ConfigEditorDialog: The shown dialog, deleted when closed.
    """
    key = id(config)
    dialog = cls._instances.get(key)
    if dialog is None:
        dialog = cls(config, parent, delete_on_close=True)
        cls._instances[key] = dialog
        dialog.destroyed.connect(lambda *_: cls._instances.pop(key, None))
    dialog.show()
    dialog.raise_()
    dialog.activateWindow()
    return dialog

def add_key(self, parent: JsonNode) -> None:
    """Ask for a key name and type, then add it to a dict node.

    Args:
        parent (JsonNode): The dict node to add the key to.
    """
    existing = {child.key for child in parent.children}
    key, ok = QtWidgets.QInputDialog.getText(self, "Add key", "Key name:")
    if not ok or not key:
        return
    if key in existing:
        QtWidgets.QMessageBox.warning(
            self, "Add key", f"Key '{key}' already exists."
        )
        return
    kind = self._ask_kind()
    if kind is not None:
        self.document.model.add_child(parent, key, nodes.default_value(kind))
        self._expand(parent)

def change_type(self, node: JsonNode, kind: Kind) -> None:
    """Replace a node's value with the default value of another type.

    Args:
        node (JsonNode): The node to convert.
        kind (Kind): The new type.
    """

        self.document.model.set_value(node, nodes.default_value(kind))
        self._expand(node)

def confirm_discard(self) -> bool:
    """Ask what to do with unsaved layers; return False if the user cancels."""
    if not self.document.is_dirty:
        return True
    Button = QtWidgets.QMessageBox.StandardButton
    names = ", ".join(self.document.dirty_layers)
    answer = QtWidgets.QMessageBox.question(
        self,
        "Unsaved changes",
        f"Save changes to: {names}?",
        Button.Save | Button.Discard | Button.Cancel,
    )
    if answer == Button.Save:
        return self.save_all()
    return answer == Button.Discard

def prompt_new_layer(self) -> None:
    """Ask for a new layer's details and register it on the config."""
    dialog = NewLayerDialog(self.document.layers, self.document.current_layer, self)
    if dialog.exec() != QtWidgets.QDialog.DialogCode.Accepted:
        return
    try:
        self.document.new_layer(*dialog.values())
    except ValueError as error:
        QtWidgets.QMessageBox.warning(self, "New layer", str(error))

def values(self) -> tuple[str, str | None, pathlib.Path | None]:
    """Return the entered values.

        tuple[str, str | None, pathlib.Path | None]: Layer name, parent layer
            name (None for a root layer) and file path (None if left empty).

        pathlib.Path(path) if path else None,

def createEditor(self, parent, option, index) -> QtWidgets.QWidget | None:
    """Create the editor matching the value's type.

    Color values open a color dialog instead and return None, as do types
    without an inline editor (dict, list, null, binary).

    Args:
        parent (QtWidgets.QWidget): Parent of the editor.
        option (QtWidgets.QStyleOptionViewItem): Style options of the cell.
        index (QtCore.QModelIndex): The cell being edited.

    Returns:
        QtWidgets.QWidget | None: The editor, or None if there is no inline editor.
    """
    kind = index.data(KIND_ROLE)
    value = index.data(QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.EditRole)
    if kind == Kind.INT:
        if abs(value) <= INT_LIMIT:
            editor = QtWidgets.QSpinBox(parent)
            editor.setRange(-INT_LIMIT - 1, INT_LIMIT)
            return editor
        editor = QtWidgets.QLineEdit(parent)
        editor.setValidator(
            QtGui.QRegularExpressionValidator(QtCore.QRegularExpression(r"-?\d+"))
        )
        return editor
    if kind == Kind.FLOAT:
        editor = QtWidgets.QDoubleSpinBox(parent)
        editor.setRange(-1e308, 1e308)
        editor.setDecimals(6)
        editor.setStepType(
            QtWidgets.QAbstractSpinBox.StepType.AdaptiveDecimalStepType
        )
        return editor
    if kind == Kind.COLOR:
        self._pick_color(parent, index, value)
        return None
    if kind == Kind.STR:
        return QtWidgets.QLineEdit(parent)
    return None

def setModelData(self, editor, model, index):
    """Write the editor's value back to the model.

    Invalid integer text is ignored.

    Args:
        editor (QtWidgets.QWidget): The editor created by createEditor.
        model (QtCore.QAbstractItemModel): The model to update.
        index (QtCore.QModelIndex): The cell being edited.
    """
    if isinstance(editor, QtWidgets.QSpinBox | QtWidgets.QDoubleSpinBox):
        editor.interpretText()
        model.setData(index, editor.value())
    elif isinstance(editor, QtWidgets.QLineEdit):
        text = editor.text()
        if index.data(KIND_ROLE) == Kind.INT:
            if not text.lstrip("-").isdigit():

            model.setData(index, text)

def filterAcceptsRow(self, source_row, source_parent) -> bool:
    """Return whether a row is visible.

    Binary rows are always hidden; other rows are shown if their key, a
    descendant's key or an ancestor's key matches the filter.

    Args:
        source_row (int): Row in the source model.
        source_parent (QtCore.QModelIndex): Parent index in the source model.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the row is shown.
    """
    index = self.sourceModel().index(source_row, KEY_COLUMN, source_parent)
    if index.data(KIND_ROLE) == Kind.BINARY:
        return False
    if super().filterAcceptsRow(source_row, source_parent):
        return True
    return self._ancestor_matches(source_parent)

def assign_at(self, path: ModelPath, value: JsonValue) -> None:
    """Replace the value (and type) of the node at *path*, rebuilding children."""
    node = self.node_at(path)
    index = self.index_for(node)
    if node.children:
        self.beginRemoveRows(index, 0, len(node.children) - 1)
        node.children = []
        self.endRemoveRows()
    count = len(value) if isinstance(value, dict | list) else 0
    if count:
        self.beginInsertRows(index, 0, count - 1)
        node.assign(value)
        self.endInsertRows()
    else:
        node.assign(value)
    last = self.index_for(node, len(COLUMNS) - 1)
    self.dataChanged.emit(self.index_for(node), last)

def data(
    self, index: QtCore.QModelIndex, role=QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.DisplayRole
) -> typing.Any:
    """Return the data of *index* for *role*.

    Besides the standard roles, KIND_ROLE returns the node's Kind and
    NODE_ROLE the JsonNode itself.

    Args:
        index (QtCore.QModelIndex): The cell.
        role (int): The item data role.

    Returns:
        Any: The data, or None if there is none for this role.
    """
    if not index.isValid():
        return None
    node, column = self.node_for(index), index.column()
    Role = QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole
    if role == KIND_ROLE:
        return node.kind
    if role == NODE_ROLE:
        return node
    if column == KEY_COLUMN and role == Role.DisplayRole:
        return str(node.key)
    if column == TYPE_COLUMN and role == Role.DisplayRole:
        return node.kind.value
    if column != VALUE_COLUMN:
        return None
    if role == Role.DisplayRole:
        return self._display_value(node)
    if role == Role.EditRole:
        return node.value
    if role == Role.CheckStateRole and node.kind is Kind.BOOL:
        return (
            QtCore.Qt.CheckState.Checked
            if node.value
            else (QtCore.Qt.CheckState.Unchecked)
        )
    if role == Role.DecorationRole and node.kind is Kind.COLOR:
        return QtGui.QColor(node.value)
    if role == Role.ForegroundRole and node.kind is Kind.NULL:
        return QtWidgets.QApplication.palette().placeholderText()
    return None

@staticmethod
def path_of(node: JsonNode) -> ModelPath:
    """Return the keys leading from the root to *node*."""
    keys: list[str | int] = []
    while node.parent is not None:
        keys.append(node.key)
        node = node.parent
    return tuple(reversed(keys))

def setData(self, index, value, role=QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.EditRole) -> bool:
    """Push an undoable edit for the value cell at *index*.

    Args:
        index (QtCore.QModelIndex): The cell; only the value column is editable.
        value (Any): The new value, or a check state for bool values.
        role (int): EditRole, or CheckStateRole for bool values.

    if not index.isValid() or index.column() != VALUE_COLUMN:
        return False

    if role == QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.CheckStateRole and node.kind is Kind.BOOL:
        value = QtCore.Qt.CheckState(value) == QtCore.Qt.CheckState.Checked
    elif role != QtCore.Qt.ItemDataRole.EditRole:
        return False
    self.set_value(node, typing.cast(JsonValue, value))
    return True

def assign(self, value: JsonValue) -> None:
    """Replace this node's content with *value* (rebuilding children)."""
    self.kind = kind_of(value)
    self.children = []
    self.value = None
    if isinstance(value, dict):

def is_binary_string(text: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether *text* looks like an encoded binary blob (base64)."""
    if len(text) < BINARY_MIN_LENGTH or len(text) % 4:
        return False
    try:

        return False
    return True

docs.text:
Classify a JSON value.

Source code in src/json_config_qt/tree/nodes.py 
def kind_of(value: JsonValue) -> Kind:
    """Classify a JSON value."""
    if value is None:
        return Kind.NULL
    if isinstance(value, bool):  # before int: bool is an int subclass
        return Kind.BOOL
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return Kind.INT
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return Kind.FLOAT
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if COLOR_RE.match(value):
            return Kind.COLOR
        if is_binary_string(value):
            return Kind.BINARY
        return Kind.STR
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return Kind.DICT
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return Kind.LIST
    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported JSON value: {value!r}")

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
json_config_qt
├── editor_dialog.py   ConfigEditorDialog: floating window around the widget
├── editor_widget.py   ConfigEditorWidget (+ NewLayerDialog): the UI and its actions
├── document.py        LayerDocument: one tree model and undo stack per layer
├── main.py            standalone launcher, config_from_files()
└── tree/
    ├── nodes.py       JsonNode, Kind: the JSON tree and value classification
    ├── model.py       JsonTreeModel: QAbstractItemModel over the nodes
    ├── commands.py    SetValue, InsertChild, RemoveChild: the undo commands
    ├── delegate.py    ValueDelegate: an editor per value type
    └── filter.py      FilterProxy: key filter, hides binary values

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
LayeredConfig ──layer.get_data()──▶ JsonTreeModel ──▶ FilterProxy ──▶ QTreeView
   ▲                                     ▲   │ setData (user edit)
   │ resolve()                           │   ▼
   │                                QUndoStack ◀── commands ── model.*_at()
   └── layer.replace_data(model.to_python()) ◀── LayerDocument.save_layer()

The editor works on the raw dict of each layer, not on the typed values. That is why it needs no ConfigValues class: it can edit keys the schema doesn't know about, and what it saves is what you saw.

docs.title: The document
docs.text:
LayerDocument(config) is the model of the editor, with no widgets.

  • model_for(name) creates a JsonTreeModel and a QUndoStack for a layer the first time it is asked for, loaded from layer.get_data(), and caches it. Switching layers therefore keeps edits and history.
  • All stacks join one QUndoGroup. set_layer makes the layer's stack the active one, so the widget's undo and redo actions follow the current layer.
  • A layer is dirty when its stack isn't clean (cleanChanged drives dirtyChanged).
  • save_layer(name) copies model.to_python() into the layer (replace_data), saves the file through the manager, marks the stack clean, calls config.resolve() and emits saved. It raises RuntimeError for a layer without a file. save_all saves the dirty layers.
  • new_layer registers a ConfigLayer on the config's manager, with at most one parent, and selects it. layers is read from config.layers every time, but the widget refreshes its selector only on layersChanged, which new_layer emits, so a layer registered elsewhere appears after the next such refresh.

Warning

The document edits a snapshot taken when a layer's model is first created. If the layer's data changes outside the editor afterwards, the editor still shows the old data, and saving overwrites the change.

docs.title: The widget and the dialog
docs.text:
ConfigEditorWidget builds its UI in _create_actions, _create_widgets, _create_layouts and _create_connections, called from __init__. The same structure is used by ConfigEditorDialog, NewLayerDialog and other widgets in the project.

  • The tree view shows FilterProxy(document.model). A change of layer swaps the source model and reapplies the header sizes (they are ignored while there are no columns).
  • Failed saves (OSError, RuntimeError) are caught in _guarded and shown in a message box; the document itself raises.
  • Actions are added to the widget with WidgetWithChildrenShortcut so the Save, Undo and Redo only work with focus inside the editor.
  • ConfigEditorDialog.show_for keeps a class-level dict {id(config): dialog}, removed when the dialog is destroyed.

docs.title: The launcher
docs.text: main.config_from_files(paths) builds one layer per file, each depending on the previous one, and a config with an empty ConfigValues. It calls ConfigLayerManager.clear() first, which drops every named manager in the process: fine for a launcher, so don't call it from application code.

docs.title: Branches and versions
docs.text:
develop is the default and PR branch; main is the release branch. Work on a feature branch named after the GitHub issue.

The version lives in VERSION and is copied into pyproject.toml (make update-version). Add a section at the top of CHANGELOG.rst for each release, one bullet per user-visible change with the issue number where there is one.

make release VERSION=1.2.3 [RELEASE_TITLE="..."]

tags main, pushes, and merges back into develop. The tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release from the changelog.

docs.title: Generated resources
docs.text: src/json_config_qt/resources/resources_rc.py is generated from resources.qrc by make qrc, and committed. make build regenerates it first. Run make qrc after changing an icon or the .qrc file.

docs.title: The json-config dependency
docs.text:
The editor depends on sowwic-json-config, the distribution of json-config (it imports as json_config). During development pyproject.toml resolves it from git through [tool.uv.sources].

Warning

[tool.uv.sources] is not part of the published metadata. A release on PyPI asks for sowwic-json-config from PyPI, so that package has to be published first. Once it is, delete the git source (or point it at the release tag) and add a lower bound to the dependency, e.g. "sowwic-json-config>=1.0.7". Do not publish with the git source still in place: the build would work and every user's install would fail.

The name json-config on PyPI belongs to a different project. Always depend on sowwic-json-config.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text:
The distribution is sowwic-json-config-qt, imported as json_config_qt. Targets come from the general/pypi module of sowwic/makefiles:

make pypi-publish-dev     # build and upload to TestPyPI
make pypi-publish         # build and upload to PyPI

Both clean and build first. uv publish reads the token from UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN, so set it for the run only:

UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN=pypi-... make pypi-publish

PyPI and TestPyPI have separate accounts and tokens. The first upload needs an account-wide token, because a project-scoped token can only exist once the project does. A published version can't be replaced: bump VERSION and publish again. To hide a bad one, yank it on pypi.org.

TestPyPI doesn't host dependencies such as PySide6, so install a test upload with --extra-index-url:

pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ \
    --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ sowwic-json-config-qt

docs.title: CI
docs.text: The workflows in .github/workflows/ call the shared ones of sowwic/gh-workflows: tests (Python 3.14, offscreen Qt, on Linux and Windows and then macOS), lint, docs deployment and release. Dependabot opens weekly PRs against develop for the lockfile and the Actions, and holds back PySide6 major versions.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
make pytest                                              # everything, with coverage
uv run pytest tests/test_tree.py::test_set_value_undo_redo   # one test
make pytest-pdb                                          # verbose, pdb on failure

make pytest runs with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, and tests/conftest.py sets it too, so no display is needed. Coverage (--cov=json_config_qt) is always on.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: File Covers tests/test_tree.py Value classification, the model round trip, undo and redo of every command, the filter proxy. tests/test_editor.py LayerDocument (layers, switching, saving, new layers), the widget, the dialog (close prompt, save button, show_for reuse, shortcuts). tests/test_package.py The package imports and a QApplication starts.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Use the qtbot fixture from pytest-qt for anything that creates a widget or a QObject, so it gets a QApplication and is cleaned up.
  • Build configs from files with config_from_files([...]) in a tmp_path, never from the repository's folders. The helper clears all ConfigLayerManager instances, so tests don't leak layers into each other.
  • Blocking dialogs (QMessageBox.question, QInputDialog) hang a test: patch them with monkeypatch, as test_dialog_close_prompts_when_dirty does.
  • Assert state, not pixels: read the model, the actions' isEnabled() and the document's dirty layers.

docs.title: What to cover
docs.text:
• A new value kind or editor: kind_of, the display text, the delegate's editor and a round trip that doesn't change the data.
  • A new edit: the command's redo and undo, and that the stack becomes clean again after undoing back to the save point.
  • Saving: that only the saved layer's file changes, and that hidden (binary) values are written back.

docs.title: Nodes and kinds
docs.text:
JsonNode(key, value, parent) is a node of the document. A container (dict or list) keeps child nodes and no value; a leaf keeps its value. assign(value) rebuilds a node, and to_python() turns a subtree back into plain JSON data.

kind_of(value) classifies a value into a Kind:

Kind Rule null None bool checked before int, since bool is a subclass of int int, float by type color a string matching ^#(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{8})$ binary a string of at least BINARY_MIN_LENGTH (64) characters, a multiple of 4 long, that decodes as strict base64 str any other string dict, list by type

Anything else (a JSON file can't hold it, but a hand-built dict could) raises TypeError. A long run of letters whose length is a multiple of 4 is therefore treated as binary; use a shorter or differently shaped string if that is not what you mean.

SWITCHABLE_KINDS are the types a user may convert to; binary is excluded. default_value(kind) gives the value a conversion or new key starts with.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
JsonTreeModel is a QAbstractItemModel with the columns Key, Value and Type.

  • Nodes are addressed by a path: the tuple of keys from the root (("style", "layers", 0)). Commands store paths, not nodes, so they stay valid after the tree is rebuilt.
  • The *_at methods (assign_at, insert_at, remove_at) change the tree and emit the right Qt signals. They are meant to be called by commands only.
  • The user-facing methods (set_value, add_child, remove_node, and setData from the views) push a command on the undo stack. set_value ignores a change to an equal value of the same type.
  • Extra roles: KIND_ROLE returns the node's Kind, NODE_ROLE the JsonNode.
  • Only the Value column is editable. Bool values use the check state role.
  • List children are renumbered after inserting or removing, and the key column of the shifted rows is refreshed.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command undo SetValue(model, path, value) Assigns the value the node had when the command was made. Also used to change a type. InsertChild(model, parent_path, row, key, value) Removes the inserted child. RemoveChild(model, path) Inserts the removed value again at its old row.

Each command captures what it needs to undo when it is created, so create it right before pushing it.

docs.title: The delegate and the proxy
docs.text:
ValueDelegate returns a QSpinBox (ints within 32 bits), a QLineEdit with an integer validator (larger ints), a QDoubleSpinBox, or a QLineEdit for strings. For a color it opens a QColorDialog from createEditor and writes the result with setData itself, then returns None, so there is no inline editor. Text that isn't an integer is ignored for an int field.

FilterProxy is a recursive QSortFilterProxyModel on the key column. filterAcceptsRow hides binary rows always, and shows a row if its key matches, a descendant's key matches (recursive filtering), or an ancestor's key matches, which is how a matching key shows its whole subtree. Hidden rows stay in the source model, which is why binary values survive a save.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who add the config editor to an application, or use it.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install sowwic-json-config-qt

Requires Python 3.14+. It installs PySide6 and sowwic-json-config; the editor works on the LayeredConfig of the latter and imports as json_config_qt.

Until a release is on PyPI, use pip install git+https://github.com/sowwic/json-config-qt.git.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Opening the dialog ConfigEditorDialog: showing it, one per config, the saved signal. Embedding the widget ConfigEditorWidget: the actions to place in your UI, shortcuts, the unsaved-changes prompt. Editing layers What the editor shows and does: types, filter, undo, new layers, and what saving writes.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Edit any JSON files from the command line. Each file is a layer that overrides the one before it, named after its file stem:

python -m json_config_qt.main base.json user.json

The launcher builds a config with no schema, so it shows exactly what is in the files.

docs.title: Opening the dialog
docs.text:
ConfigEditorDialog is a floating, non-modal window editing every layer of a LayeredConfig. A host application opens it, usually from a menu action:

from json_config_qt.editor_dialog import ConfigEditorDialog

def open_settings(self):
    dialog = ConfigEditorDialog.show_for(self.config, parent=self)
    dialog.saved.connect(self.on_layer_saved)

show_for(config, parent=None) shows the dialog and brings it to the front. It keeps one dialog per config: calling it again while the dialog is open raises the same window instead of opening another, so a menu action can call it without checking. The dialog deletes itself when closed.

saved is emitted with the layer name after a layer was written. The config has already been resolved again by then, so config.values is up to date:

def on_layer_saved(self, layer_name: str):
    self.apply_theme(self.config.values.theme)

Because show_for returns the same dialog while it is open, connecting after every call would connect your slot again each time, and it would run once per call. Connect with UniqueConnection to a bound method, which ignores a repeated connection:

dialog = ConfigEditorDialog.show_for(self.config, parent=self)
dialog.saved.connect(self.on_layer_saved, QtCore.Qt.ConnectionType.UniqueConnection)

A closed dialog is deleted, so the next show_for makes a new one and you connect again.

docs.title: Creating one yourself
docs.text:
dialog = ConfigEditorDialog(config, parent=window, delete_on_close=False)
dialog.show()

Use the constructor when you want to keep the dialog and reopen it. dialog.editor is the ConfigEditorWidget inside it and dialog.document its LayerDocument.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• The window title shows the current layer and a * while any layer has unsaved edits.
  • The buttons at the bottom are Save Layer, Save All, Undo, Redo and Close.
  • Closing it with unsaved edits asks whether to save, discard or cancel.
  • It is non-modal, so the host stays usable.

Note

show_for identifies a config by the Python object (id(config)). Two config objects for the same layers get two dialogs, and they won't see each other's edits until saved.

docs.title: What you see
docs.text:
A selector lists every layer of the config in dependency order, with its file and a * while it has unsaved edits. Hover an entry for its file and the layers it depends on. Below it, a filter box and a tree with three columns: Key, Value and Type.

Each layer shows its own data only, not the merged result. A layer whose file holds just {"level": 20} shows one row.

docs.title: Value types
docs.text:
The editor decides the type of each value from its content:

Type Editor Notes dict, list none The value column shows the item count. Add and remove through the context menu. bool check box int spin box Integers beyond 32 bits get a text field with digits only. float spin box Six decimals. str text field color color dialog A string like #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. The alpha channel is offered only if the value has one. binary hidden A base64 string of at least 64 characters. null none Shown in italics.

Double-click a value (or press the edit key) to change it. A bool toggles in place.

Note

Binary values are hidden from the tree, not removed. They stay in the layer and are written back when you save.

docs.title: Context menu
docs.text:
Right-click the tree:

  • Add key… on a dict (or on empty space for the top level), asks for a key and a type. A key that exists already is refused.
  • Append item… on a list.
  • Change type replaces the value with the default of another type (0, "", false, #ffffff, an empty list or dict, or null).
  • Remove deletes the key or item. Later list items are renumbered.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text: Type in the filter box to show only keys containing the text, case-insensitively. A match keeps its parents visible and shows its whole subtree, and matches are expanded.

docs.title: Undo and redo
docs.text: Every edit (value, add, remove, change type) is one undoable step. Each layer has its own history, which is kept while you switch layers: undo goes back through the edits of the layer you are looking at. A layer is clean again when you undo back to where it was saved.

docs.title: New layers
docs.text:
New layer… asks for:

  • a name, which must be unique,
  • the layer it depends on, or none for a root layer,
  • an optional file. The name is filled from the file name if empty.

The new layer is registered on the config and selected. A layer without a file can be edited but not saved: saving it shows an error.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Save Layer writes the current layer, Save All every layer with edits.

The editor writes exactly the layer's data as shown. That differs from LayeredConfig.save(), which removes values equal to what lower layers provide. Here an override you wrote stays, even if it equals the inherited value, so you decide what a layer holds.

After a save the config is resolved again, so config.values reflects the new files, and the dialog's saved signal is emitted with the layer name. The file is written as JSON with four-space indentation.

If the write fails, an error dialog shows the reason and the layer stays dirty.

docs.title: Embedding the widget
docs.text:
To put the editor inside your own window, or to use your own buttons, embed ConfigEditorWidget:

from json_config_qt.editor_widget import ConfigEditorWidget

editor = ConfigEditorWidget(config, parent=self)
layout.addWidget(editor)
editor.saved.connect(self.on_layer_saved)

The widget has the layer selector, the filter box and the tree. It has no menus or buttons of its own for saving and history: it exposes them as QActions that you place where you like.

Action Does save_action Save the current layer (the standard Save shortcut). save_all_action Save every layer with unsaved edits. new_layer_action Ask for a name, parent and file, and add a layer. undo_action, redo_action Undo and redo in the current layer. expand_all_action, collapse_all_action Expand or collapse the tree. 
toolbar.addAction(editor.save_action)
toolbar.addAction(editor.undo_action)
edit_menu.addAction(editor.redo_action)

The undo and redo actions follow the layer being edited, and show the text of the command they would run.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Save, Undo and Redo have standard key sequences, but they only apply while the editor has focus (WidgetWithChildrenShortcut), so they never fight with the shortcuts of the host. If you want an application-wide shortcut, set it on your own copy of the action.

docs.title: Unsaved changes
docs.text:
Call confirm_discard() from your own close handling:

def closeEvent(self, event):
    if self.editor.confirm_discard():
        event.accept()
    else:
        event.ignore()

It returns True at once when nothing is dirty. Otherwise it asks to save, discard or cancel, and returns False on cancel, or when a save fails.

docs.title: Saving from code
docs.text:
editor.save_current()   # True when written; an error dialog is shown on failure
editor.save_all()

Both show a dialog and return False on a failed write instead of raising. For headless use, work with editor.document (LayerDocument), where save_layer(name) and save_all() raise.
